review: 2:1–2:2 יֶשׁ־לָנוּ שֻׁתָּפוּת … בָּאוֹר לִפְנֵי־אֵל — the Arabic لَنَا اشْتِرَاكٌ مَعَكَ فِي النُّورِ أَمَامَ الْآبِ is 1 John 1:3–5; the Hebrew keeps שֻׁתָּפוּת (the glossary term) with the light and the 'before the Father', because the stanza's whole claim is access.

3:1–3:2 כָּל־אֲשֶׁר לָאָב לְךָ … אֵין־לוֹ קֵץ — John 16:15 (כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לָאָב שֶׁלִּי הוּא) with John 3:34; the Hebrew keeps the verbless clause, so the sharing stays a statement of fact rather than an inheritance transaction.

4:3 בָּהּ שִׁתַּפְתָּ גוּפְךָ — the Arabic أَشْرَكْتَ فِيهِ جَسَدَك is 'You shared Your body in it' (i.e. in that love); the Hebrew keeps גּוּף, the word the epistle uses for the incarnate body (Col 1:22), rather than the more general בָּשָׂר used for 'flesh'.

5:2 אֶת־הַכָּבוֹד אֲשֶׁר קָנִיתָ — the Arabic الْمَجْدَ الَّذِي اكْتَسَبْتَهُ is 'the glory You acquired'; קָנָה is the glossary verb for acquiring (Exod 15:16), so the line keeps the sense of a purchase rather than a reward.

6:1–6:2 אַךְ בִּכְבוֹדְךָ … שָׁוֶה אַתָּה לָאָב — the Arabic تُعَادِلُ الْآبَ بِهِ is 'You equal the Father in it'; the Hebrew states equality with no softening adverb, since the stanza is the hymn's one explicit doctrinal line.
